conviction_note: Evidence is balanced: AEC software counterparties and peers that reported after Autodesk's 27 Aug guide were healthy-to-strong and management said its guide embeds prudence (likely beat), but the bar has been lifted (whisper $3.16 above the $3.09 guide top, two bullish sell-side moves and a +6.9% 20-day run-up), the euro fell ~3.5% from the guide date which mutes any FY raise, cRPO is guided to keep decelerating, and this name sold its last two beat-and-raises (-4.0%, -3.67%); so p_up 49 on an 8.0% abs move gives -0.16, against a findings sum of -0.95 that is driven by many small proxies rather than one decisive number.
bar: Q3 FY27 company guide revenue $2,125-2,140M, non-GAAP EPS $3.04-3.09 (8-K exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000769397/000076939726000059/q227pressrelease.htm, 2026-08-27); consensus $2.13B revenue / $3.07 EPS, near guide midpoint, Earnings Whisper $3.16 (https://finviz.com/news/423384/autodesk-s-raised-outlook-faces-its-first-test-as-maintainx-joins-the-numbers, 2026-11-16). FY27 guide billings $8,575-8,650M, revenue $8,295-8,345M, non-GAAP EPS $12.52-12.60, ~39% non-GAAP margin. Benzinga lists an EPS estimate of $2.91 that disagrees with both and is treated as stale. No sourced Q3 billings or cRPO consensus. Autodesk beat the high end of its revenue and EPS guide in Q1 and Q2 FY27; print_vs_bar +0.9% assumes revenue of about $2.15B against $2.13B.
positioning_check: Short interest about 9.2M shares, 4.4% of shares outstanding, 6.1 days to cover at the 2026-11-13 settlement, rising about 1.4% month on month (https://equibles.com/stocks/adsk/shortinterest); AltIndex 9.38M / 4.49%, up 12.4%, 4.57 days (https://altindex.com/ticker/adsk/short-interest). Elevated for ADSK but not crowded. Baseline skew +3.57 vol points (25d put over call), so downside is paid; put/call OI 0.93; event-implied move 8.17% (straddle 8.73%), ATM spread 17% of mid. Spot $258.84, +6.9% over 20 days, +1.4% over 5 days, -16.6% from the 52-week high. Sell-side leaning bullish into the print: Jefferies raised its target from $300 to $325 on 2026-11-09 expecting a clean Q3; Loop Capital upgraded to Buy on 2026-11-13. AAII counts one downgrade and no upgrades in the month to 11-23 (source not identified).

findings.finding: AEC/construction software counterparties and peers that reported after Autodesk's 27 Aug guide were healthy to strong. Bentley (5 Nov): Q3 ARR +13% cc, all organic, record 110% net revenue retention, 2026 ARR growth guide raised to 12.5-13.5% from 10.5-12.5%. Procore (early Nov): Q3 revenue +19%, organic growth accelerating for a third quarter, FY raised, RPO +28%, stock +11%. Trimble AECO ARR +13% organic (4 Nov). Autodesk said construction is growing above 20%, and AECO is 50% of its revenue ($1,029M of $2,046M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autodesk beat the high end of its revenue guide in Q2 FY27 (revenue +16%, $2.046B against $2.01B consensus) and fell 3.67%. In Q1 FY27 it beat and fell 4.0%. Beats on the reported quarter have not been paid for on the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is peer evidence, not Autodesk's own number. Consensus revenue still sits at the guide midpoint ($2.13B), not above it as it would if peer strength had been carried into Autodesk estimates. Partly priced through the +6.9% 20-day run-up.
findings.independence: Procore Q3 2026: https://finviz.com/news/415677/procore-beats-as-organic-growth-accelerates-for-a-third-straight-quarter-but-the-dronedeploy-deal-changes-the-balance-sheet. Trimble AECO ARR +13% organic: https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024760/trmb-q3-earnings-meet-estimates-as-aeco-growth-lifts-revenues. These are three separate companies' documents. The readings are proxies: none is Autodesk's own channel.

findings.finding: Manufacturing-design peers were steady. Dassault Systemes (28 Oct) raised its 2026 objectives for the first time in two years: revenue growth narrowed to 4-5% cc and operating margin raised to 32.5-32.7%. PTC (4 Nov) reported ARR excluding divested units +8% (9.7% cc) and beat on EPS. Autodesk MFG was $385M (+15%) of Q2 revenue, about 19%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autodesk no longer breaks out Design/Make from Q3, and MFG has not been the line its reactions turned on. Same history as above: beats sold on the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A small segment read through from peers that is not in Autodesk-specific previews. It is at most a marginal driver, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: PTC FY26 Q4: https://finviz.com/news/415751/ptc-announces-fourth-fiscal-quarter-and-full-fiscal-year-2026-results (a different company and document).

findings.finding: Nemetschek, the closest listed AEC design peer, reported organic growth of 13.7% (ex-HCSS) and ARR +35.8% including the acquisition, kept its 2026 outlook (organic revenue +14-15% cc), and the stock fell more than 8% on the release. The peer reaction function into this season is selling solid AEC design prints that do not raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autodesk itself fell 3.67% and 4.0% on its last two beat-and-raise prints, the same pattern.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction pattern rather than a fact the market could price ahead of time. If it were fully expected, skew would be more extreme than +3.6.
findings.independence: Nemetschek outlook held (MarketBeat call highlights, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-nemetschek-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-05/). Same event, so it counts once.

findings.finding: The AIA Architecture Billings Index was 44.9 in October 2026 (44.7 in September): continued contraction, newly signed design contracts still declining, and soft conditions in every region. This is an end-market series for AutoCAD/Revit seat demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ABI has been below 50 for more than four years while Autodesk AECO revenue grew 15-17%. The stock has not traded on it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and long-running, so it is largely priced. It is filed as an independent series that cuts against the peer software strength.
findings.independence: September ABI 44.7: https://aia.org/resource-center/abi-september-2026-architecture-firm-billings-slump-deepens. It is contradicted in direction by the broader AEC software series (Bentley, Procore, Trimble ARR), so it is sized below them.

findings.finding: The euro fell from about $1.165 when Autodesk set its guide (24-27 Aug) to about $1.136 at the 30 Sep close and about $1.12 at the end of October (a 15-month low of 1.1113 on 14 Oct), roughly -3.5%. EMEA is 39% of revenue ($804M of $2,046M in Q2, where FX added 6 points: +19% reported against +13% cc). That is a translation headwind to Q3 billings and, more importantly, to Q4 and the FY27 revenue/billings guide at current rates, muting any pass-through of a Q3 beat into a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27: the stock fell about 4% when the FY EPS midpoint ($12.56) landed below consensus ($12.60) despite the beat. A guide that does not raise by the full beat has been punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (finviz 11-16, Jefferies) discuss MaintainX, organic growth and Western Europe but not FX. Autodesk hedges part of its exposure and recognises revenue largely from deferred balances booked at older rates, so the effect is muted and unconfirmed by the company. That is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Late-August level ~1.165: https://www.fxstreet.com/news/euro-holds-above-mid-11600s-vs-usd-looks-to-us-pce-data-for-fresh-impetus-202608260754. EMEA FX tailwind in Q2 from the company 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000769397/000076939726000059/q227pressrelease.htm. Macro-to-company transmission that is not confirmed by Autodesk.

findings.finding: Autodesk's own 8-K says it is reducing multi-year discounts and winding down multi-year maintenance-to-subscription renewals, which 'temporarily weighs on unbilled deferred revenue and RPO growth'. Q2 cRPO growth already slowed to 12% (from 18-20%), total RPO to +2% and unbilled deferred revenue to -8%. Another deceleration in cRPO/RPO is the likely headline metric in Q3 and the one the stock sold on in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: cRPO decelerating to 12% was cited as a reason for the 3.67-4% fall despite a revenue/EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The company disclosed the mechanism, so the direction is known. What is not priced is the size of the next step down; there is no sourced cRPO consensus. If it were fully priced, previews would quote a cRPO bar, and none does.
findings.independence: Finviz 2026-08-28 says the effect lasts 'several more quarters': https://finviz.com/news/386537/autodesk-shares-fall-as-fiscal-2027-earnings-guidance-trails-expectations-despite-q2-beat. Shares a source with the company filing.

findings.finding: The bar has risen into the print. Earnings Whisper is $3.16, above the $3.09 top of the company's EPS guide and the $3.07 consensus. Jefferies lifted its target from $300 to $325 (9 Nov) expecting a 'clean' Q3, and Loop Capital upgraded to Buy (13 Nov). The stock is +6.9% over 20 days and traded as high as $279 in November. An in-line or modest beat lands under the buy-side bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints beat consensus and fell 3.67% and 4.0%. Before that: +5.32%, +2.36%, +9.09%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positive skew (+3.57) already says downside is paid, so this is partly priced. What is not reflected is that the whisper sits above the guide's top while consensus sits at its midpoint, so the 'beat' headline will be judged against a higher number than the wire carries.

findings.finding: Autodesk used its Q3 call last year to give early color on the next year (Nov 2025: FY27 billings tailwinds from the new transaction model 'will significantly diminish'). On the Q2 FY27 call the CFO said FY28 will not get the transaction-model tailwind, that the FY28 non-GAAP margin improves only 'modestly' from 39% while MaintainX's losses annualise, and that the FY29 41% target is unchanged. FY27 also carries the largest EBA renewal cohort, concentrated in Q4. Preliminary FY28 framing is the likely swing factor and a new period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (Nov 2025), when FY27 headwinds were flagged early: +2.36%. Q2 FY27, when the FY EPS guide was slightly below the Street: about -4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street has no company FY28 number. 'Modest' margin improvement with an unprofitable acquisition annualising sits below where an activist-era investor base anchored. The sign is genuinely uncertain, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Precedent of early next-year color at Q3: https://www.aol.com/articles/autodesk-adsk-q3-2026-earnings-232043681.html (a different document).

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call that the FY27 guide 'embeds some prudence against our expectations of sales productivity normalization', that Q2 billings linearity was 'better than we expected', that construction grows above 20%, and that sellers were closer to plan in most regions. The Q3 guide was set after two quarters of beating its own high end, so a revenue/EPS beat above the $2.140B / $3.09 top is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats above the guide's high end in Q1 and Q2 FY27 were followed by -4.0% and -3.67%. The beat itself has not been the line that pays.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($2.13B) and EPS ($3.07) still sit at the guide midpoint rather than at the top, so the sell-side has not modelled the habitual beat. The whisper ($3.16) has, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 beat versus guide and consensus: https://finviz.com/news/386537/autodesk-shares-fall-as-fiscal-2027-earnings-guidance-trails-expectations-despite-q2-beat. Shares the transcript with the FY28 finding but is a different statement.

findings.finding: Western Europe is lagging in new-business productivity after the sales reorganisation (management, Q2 call). The AEC business changed leader in the quarter: Diana Colella was named EVP on 6 Oct, succeeding Amy Bunszel, who stayed until 2 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print turned on either item.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. It is filed because a Western Europe shortfall compounds the FX finding in the EMEA billings line.
findings.independence: Western Europe lag from the Q2 call: https://singjupost.com/transcript-autodesk-adsk-q2-fy27-earnings-call-conference/

findings.finding: Autodesk issued $1.0B of senior notes on 10 Sep 2026 ($500M 5.05% due 2029, $500M 5.65% due 2033, expected A3). The proceeds repay the $1.0B term loan of 15 Jun 2026 that funded MaintainX. The money buys a refinancing of an acquisition already inside the guide, so the sign is neutral.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Filed for completeness as the only 8-K since the Q2 release.

outside_window.finding: The Q4 FY27 largest-ever EBA renewal cohort is concentrated in Q4 (ends 31 Jan 2027), so its outcome is only visible at the Q4 print. The Q3 call may comment on it, which is covered by the FY28 guidance finding.
Pricing, licensing and regional rollout of Autodesk's next-generation agentic AI experience are deferred to 2027 (AU 2026).

baseline_tension: Net slightly negative, which agrees with the +3.57 put skew and leans against the +6.9% 20-day run-up. The skew already pays for the downside, so p_up is held near 50 rather than leaning harder.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last two beats): AEC peer strength cut from +0.8 to +0.5 and the management-prudence beat from +0.6 to +0.4.

Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series): ABI cut from -0.3 to -0.15 because the broader AEC software ARR series points the other way. FX, an unconfirmed macro-to-company transmission, cut from -0.5 to -0.4. The Nemetschek peer-reaction proxy cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 7 checked: short interest 4.4% / 6.1 days is not crowded, and the negatives agree with the skew, so nothing changed.
Rule 4 checked: the notes refinance MaintainX's term loan, an acquisition already in the guide, so the finding stays at 0.
